title: Going the Extra Mile: What Taxi Rides Tell Us About the Long-Hour Culture in Finance
year_note: Batch lists 2021; DOI suffix 2023.4774 suggests 2023 publication. Not verified (no article text).
near_miss_reason: Every reported DiD column includes the 'Post-policy' main effect af = 1(week > bank's policy date), where control banks get a simulated common date (1 Jan 2014). With year-week FE this is algebraically an extra regressor policy1 x 1(week > 2014w1), so the policy-bank x post coefficient is identified only off timing deviations from the common date (extra treatment regressor). Taxi Table 3 adds intern-week triple interactions; analyst Tables 4-5 add firm-by-quarter-of-year FE, an age control, and use fake data.
eligible_reason: Staggered binary design exists: 7 banks adopt 'protected weekend' policies at 7 distinct weeks (GS 2013-11-08, JPM 2014-01-01, BAML 2014-01-10, CS 2014-01-18, Citi 2014-02-07, Barclays 2014-02-28, DB 2014-04-09); 3 never-treated banks (MS, HSBC, UBS) in the taxi data. But no reported column is a plain TWFE (see near_miss_reason).
design_notes: TaxiDataCodesandFiles/Final_Code_Taxi_Data.R + analysis_functions.R. lm_did_policy (Table 2): rides from residential destinations are collapsed to bank x location (bank building vs surroundings) x year-week shares of rides in a time slot; diff = 100*(bank share - surroundings share); felm(diff ~ policy1*af | yrwk | 0 | yrwk). Unit = bank (10), time = yrwk (year*100 + week). Only a policy-group dummy (policy1), no bank FE. af = 1(yrwk > yrwk_policy) with yrwk_policy the bank's own policy week (controls: simulated 2014w1). Because af = policy1*af + (1-policy1)*1(yrwk>201401) and the common post dummy is absorbed by yrwk FE, the af main effect is equivalent to policy1 x 1(yrwk>201401). Table 2 Panel A (weekend: Fri 6-8, Fri 8-10, Fri 10-12, Sat, Sun) and Panel B (weekday evening slots 6-8, 8-10, 10-12, 12-2, 2-4): 10 regressions. Table 3 (lm_did_id) adds intern-week (summer weeks 23-32) x policy x post triple differences. Figure 2 is descriptive. Analyst part (Final_Code_Analyst_Data.R): Table 4 (absolute forecast error) and Table 5 (herding) felm(var ~ policyVsall*af | permno_quarter [+ ym] + analys [+age]); col 1 has no time FE, col 2 adds ym, cols 3-4 add age (time-varying) and col 4 replaces analyst FE by firm x analyst FE; all have firm x quarter-of-year FE (permno_quarter) and the same af main effect. Figure 3 runs subgroup regressions by analyst experience with permno_quarter + ym FE only.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 7 policy banks with 7 distinct policy weeks (Nov 2013-Apr 2014); 3 controls with simulated date 2014-01-01 in the taxi file (4 incl. BNYM in the analyst file).

screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). No regression inventory existed; read code directly. FLAG FOR LEAD: the exclusion rests on the algebra that a bank-specific 'Post-policy' main effect with a common simulated date for controls is equivalent, under year-week FE, to a policy-group x post-Jan-2014 regressor (the af coefficient is identified in the shipped full-data Table 4 output with ym FE, confirming it is not absorbed). If the lead treats af as a harmless main effect, taxi Table 2 yields 10 static specs on real data, but with only 10 banks (7 treated, 3 never-treated) the leverage screen (>=10 effective clusters, max share <=0.25) would likely bind under bank clustering; the paper clusters by week.
